h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, ט״ו Ki Seitzei, 15
Moshe Rabbi Akiva and Their Distinct Portions in Oral Torah

p: he found the Holy One, Blessed is He,
sitting and tying crowns onto the letters.
who is holding back Your hand?'
at the end of several generations,
and Akiva ben Yosef is his name,
'Master of the world, show him to me.'
at the end of eight rows,
When he reached a certain matter,
'It is a halachah given to Moshe at Sinai.'
His mind was set at ease."
Now this needs to be understood:
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
even by the students of Rabbi Akiva?
Also, why was his mind set at ease
that he heard about one matter
that it is a halachah to Moshe from Sinai?
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, knew
that he was bringing it down to earth
and that it would be called by his name.
that when Moshe Rabbeinu was born
the whole house was filled with light;
he never corrupted anything at all,
the aspect of the Written Torah;
for at the time of the Giving of the Torah
before the blemish of Adam HaRishon;
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah," etc.,
there was need for the "much wisdom,"
to rectify through it the "much vexation."
for it says in the Midrash Rabbah
they said that the Holy One, Blessed is He, concurred
well done that you broke them."
And this follows what they said
and as we said (in the previous maamar),
which comes to rectify the "much vexation,"
so that it becomes clear that so it was
since the six days of Creation.
that through this he would attain
the aspect of the Oral Torah.
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
even apart from the rectification of much vexation,
And it is related from the holy Arizal, of blessed memory,
the root of the Oral Torah,
and he is the aspect of "Malchus is the mouth;
we call it the Oral Torah."
"My word shall distill like the dew":
is also the words of the living God,
nevertheless to the sage who originates it
that he originates it on his own;
only when one sees that the ground is moist
does one know that dew has fallen.
וְהָרַמְבַּ״ן זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (בָּבָא בַתְרָא יב, א)
And the Ramban, of blessed memory (Bava Basra 12a),
כָּתַב שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
wrote that it is through ruach hakodesh
that one arrives on his own reasoning
at the words of the living God,
"and does he not give a reason?";
and this is called the crown of Torah,
and this was the portion of Rabbi Akiva.

אֲבָל הֲלֹא גַּם הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
But is not the Oral Torah too
"If a matter be hidden from you," etc.,
"and you shall come to the Kohanim, the Levi'im,
And they have already raised the question:
where do we find regarding Moshe Rabbeinu
that they should ask and expound," etc.,
as is written at the end of Megillah (32a)?
we do not find that Moshe decreed at all.
Also, why does the Gemara not mention
the decrees of the Men of the Great Assembly,
the enactments of the Men of the Great Assembly
if there were a beis din
that there is no beis din
that would be greater than they;
עַל יְדֵי בֵּית דִּין שֶׁגָּדוֹל מֵהֶם
by a beis din greater than they.
Not so the decrees of Moshe,
for no other prophet arose like Moshe.
And although regarding Mashiach it is written (Yeshayahu 52:13):
"He shall be exalted and lifted up,"
and it is expounded (Tanchuma, end of Parshas Toldos; Toldos 14):
yet it says in the holy Zohar:
only that then his level will be higher;
that the halachos were handed to Moshe;
and what was handed to Moshe,
that he wrote down in writing.
Rather, what was handed to Moshe was the power
to expound from the Torah with his pilpul
and to bring forth the halachos,
Moshe conducted himself with it generously
and gave it to Yisrael, etc.;
rather, it refers only to the pilpul."

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַתְרָא יב, א)
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Bava Basra 12a):
"And a sage is superior to a prophet, etc.
for a great man says something,
and it is then said in the name
of another great man just as he said it.
the two of them are sons of one mazal."
as is written in the holy Zohar
that they do not depend on merit
which is the Holy Ancient One;
that is, the aspect of the tip of the Yud,
which is above the Name Havayah;
אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חָזוּ
"Even though they themselves did not see,
Know that this is so, etc.,
and it is then said in the name
of Rabbi Akiva ben Yosef just as he said it";
that he is of one mazal
who was the root of the Oral Torah.
for Rabbi Akiva was the root
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה
for each one has a portion in the Torah,
and because of this he can arrive at it.
as a halachah to Moshe from Sinai just as he said it";
and about this it cannot be said
"And the man Moshe was very humble,
for he was as one who is not,
and through this he merited the wisdom
that shines into him from Keser Elyon
through the tip of the Yud.
to expound this with his pilpul from Sinai;
but to him, the later sage, there was handed down
only a halachah without any reason,
for which no reason need be given."
that were said to Moshe from Sinai
and does it not need a reason?"
as Rashi explains it as a question:
"And does it not need a reason,
like a halachah to Moshe from Sinai?"
"But perhaps it is like a blind man at a window?"
"And does he not give a reason?";
and presumably he arrived at it
And perhaps the reason Rabbi Akiva merited
to be the root of the Oral Torah
is that he was the son of converts,
"Rabbi Akiva went down before the ark, etc.,
rather, this one passes over his traits
and that one does not pass over his traits";
good from the outset by nature
who was the son of converts
and was born with bad traits,
the root of the Oral Torah,
which is to rectify the "much vexation,"
in the beginning of the Thought.
and the head of the tefillin
is on the skull, over the brain.
For the root of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
(Rabbah and Tanchuma on Chukas; Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6, Tanchuma Chukas 8):
"Things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues;
'and every precious thing his eye has seen' (Iyov 28:10)
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
the Holy One, Blessed is He,
and who is holding back Your hand?"
which are the crown of Torah,
רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם הַרְאֵהוּ לִי וְכוּלֵּי
"Master of the world, show him to me," etc.;
וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מַה הוּא אוֹמֵר
"and he did not know what he was saying";
for this was not his portion
that comes to rectify the "much vexation."
And this is the crown of Torah:
that one arrives at it and merits it
which joins the attributes of Chochmah and Binah,
which is the inwardness of Keser Elyon:
in the beginning of the Thought,
he merited his own Oral Torah,
בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
the Oral Torah of Rabbi Akiva,
which came specifically after the sin
and to merit sensing the taste in it,
how it is included in the Written Torah
זֶה לֹא הָיָה חֵלֶק מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
this was not the portion of Moshe Rabbeinu,
since he had never corrupted anything at all.
from our holy Rebbe of Izhbitza,
may the memory of the tzaddik be a blessing,
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה טז, ב)
All my days I would read
and for this reason was called "rochel,"
and after the teshuvah he did,
which he could not have known before.
And so Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
for he could not sense the taste
that Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues sensed,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לָזֶה
since he had no connection to it.
as he had heard from Sinai
(מְגִילָּה יט, ב וּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז)
that the Ancient of Days concealed
that is, to sense the taste in the Torah,
'It is a halachah to Moshe from Sinai'";
had understanding and reason in it,
and he brought them forth from his pilpul at Sinai,
for he was humbler than all men;
like a halachah without a reason.
Then his mind was set at ease,
for he saw that his own mind was high,
from a place far higher than this,
מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
than the Oral Torah of Rabbi Akiva,
which is only to rectify the "much vexation."
And so we find in the Gemara (Shabbos 89a):
"He found the Holy One, Blessed is He,
tying crowns onto the letters, etc.:
'And now, let the strength of Hashem be great,
that allude to the Oral Torah,
the aspect of the upper Shechinah,
as is written in the Tikkunim,
And as for His saying to him,
what help is applicable, so to speak,
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים סח, לה)
But it follows what is said (Tehillim 68:35):
an arousal from below is needed first;
and the light shines to Chochmah
which is alluded to in the tip of the Yud,
which is a tag and a crown.
And immediately he said to Him:
"And now, let the koach of Hashem be great"
the bestowal of the Oral Torah.
And it appears that this was right
at the time of his ascent
that he found Him tying, etc.;
And the reason they wrote it
in the passage of the Spies
is because the holiness of the Land
יֵשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
is connected to the Oral Torah
